newsitem.title: UK: UK resumes normal relations with Raufoss.
newsitem.headline: UK resumes normal relations with Raufoss.

text.p: The Ministry of Defence said on Thursday it has resumed normal commercial relations with Norway's Raufoss AS, which had been suspended following its involvement in a corruption case.

Junior minister John Spellar said in a parliamentary written answer that Raufoss became eligible to be considered for MoD orders from June last year under a settlement reached in the case involving civil servant Gordon Foxley.
But normal commercial relations were not to be resumed for some months while the operation of the agreement was monitored.

"The company has continued to cooperate fully with my Department since that date, including provision of full access to their relevant accounting records, and has satisfied my Department in respect of its management arrangements and approach to future contracts," Spellar said.
"We have therefore decided to resume normal commercial relations with the company."
Foxley, a former director of munitions procurement at the Ministry, was given a four-year jail sentence for taking bribes for setting up defence contracts.
"Discussions are continuing with the other companies involved in the Foxley case, against whom proceedings are still in train," Spellar said.
